episode_title: 15. Rental Market Seasonality: How the Time of Year Impacts Your Rental Property

real_qa.q: Why does rental market seasonality differ between June 1st and December 1st vacancies in Fort Worth?
real_qa.r: The rental market changes significantly throughout the year based on seasonality. A property vacant on June 1st hits peak season with higher rental prices and multiple applicants, while one vacant on December 1st faces winter slowdown with fewer applicants and longer vacancy periods. Summer is peak season because school is out and families prefer to move then, while winter is the slowest time due to extreme weather, holidays, and financial constraints from holiday spending.

real_qa.q: How much did First Choice Property Management's rental activity decline from June to July 2024?
real_qa.r: First Choice rented 22 properties in June but only 8 properties in July, with applications down by more than 50% despite using the exact same marketing strategy, photos, and pricing. Average days on market increased from 23 days to 30 days, and available properties jumped from 17 on market in June to about 30 by August, indicating a significant market cooldown.
real_qa.requete: First Choice Property Management June July 2024 rentals

real_qa.q: What are the main reasons for seasonal changes in the Fort Worth rental market?
real_qa.r: School schedules are the primary driver—summer is peak season because school is out and families can move without interrupting school semesters. Weather is critical: winter brings extreme conditions and snowmageddon events in DFW, discouraging moves. Holidays also reduce winter demand because people are preoccupied with Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's celebrations, and their discretionary income goes to holiday spending rather than rental deposits. Job relocations tend to occur in the first half of the year and summertime, and marriages typically happen in spring and fall in Texas due to moderate weather.
real_qa.requete: why rental market seasonality school weather holidays

real_qa.q: What marketing and pricing strategies should landlords use in fall versus summer?
real_qa.r: Summer is peak season where landlords get the highest rental prices and find tenants quickest with minimal strategy adjustments. Fall requires changing your marketing strategy because you need to find a renter before winter—the hardest time of year—arrives. Fall becomes nerve-wracking as landlords race to place tenants before November, December, and January. First Choice proactively moved up their fall protocol earlier in the year to adapt to 2024's shifted market conditions.
real_qa.requete: landlord marketing strategy fall summer seasonality

real_qa.q: Why is winter the best time for real estate investors to purchase rental properties?
real_qa.r: Winter is the slowest season in the sales market, which puts pressure on sellers. As a buyer, winter offers the best deals with the lowest sales prices, more concessions from sellers, and significantly more leverage in negotiations. While winter is terrible for landlords trying to rent properties, it is an ideal opportunity for investors to acquire rental properties at favorable terms.
